propositions: Local status changes are silently reverted by reconciler when a reopen occurs within one pass after rebar's own outbound push of a different status, because the baseline snapshot is advanced from the pass-start fetch rather than the last-synced value, making local==baseline false claim local is unchanged for exactly one pass.

The guard at outbound_field_diff._suppressed_by_inbound (ADR 0026 Decision 1) premises that local==baseline means local did not change since sync, but this is false in the pass where rebar itself pushes a status: the baseline holds the old value while Jira holds the new value rebar just sent.

A reopen (revert to previous status value) equals the stale baseline so outbound omits status; inbound then reads Jira's pushed value and overwrites local unchecked, while other fields from the same pass (like description) survive because they differ from baseline and are pushed outbound.

Per-mutation success must gate baseline advance, not pass exit code, because status transitions can soft-fail (RuntimeError from unreachable transition, comment-fallback 400) while the pass still exits 0; advancing baseline on a soft-fail records a sync that never happened.

The ABA exposure affects all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) because they all share the _suppressed_by_inbound guard and therefore the same false-premise defect.

Option A fix: overlay the values rebar actually pushed onto the pass-start snapshot before set_baseline records it, making baseline mean last-synced (fetch + confirmed outbound) rather than last-fetched, gated on per-mutation success tracked through the applier.
